materials.name: Stirge Proboscis
materials.desc: A hollow, needle-fine beak the length of a finger, ridged inside like a drinking straw. Leeches and field-surgeons use it to draw fluid from a wound without widening it.

materials.name: Stirge Blood Bladder
materials.desc: A thin, rubbery sac that swells like a ripe plum when the stirge has fed. Emptied and dried it becomes a squeezable pipette-bulb that never leaks.

materials.name: Allosaurus Tooth
materials.desc: A serrated, backward-curving blade of enamel as long as a dagger. Hunters set them into clubs and knuckle-guards for a vicious tearing bite.

materials.name: Allosaurus Sprint-Claw
materials.desc: A hooked foot-claw worn smooth on its underside from running down prey. Charm-makers believe it lends a burst of reckless speed.

materials.name: Allosaurus Hide
materials.desc: Pebbly, olive-brown skin, tough but flexible. Good for boots and saddles.

materials.name: Ankylosaurus Tail Club
materials.desc: A fused knot of bone the size of a keg, heavy enough to shatter a wagon wheel. Smiths build maul-heads and battering rams around it.

materials.name: Ankylosaurus Osteoderms
materials.desc: Plate-sized studs of bone that grow in the beast's skin like cobbles in a road. Armourers rivet them onto leather for near-steel protection.

materials.name: Archelon Shell Plate
materials.desc: A broad, leathery-edged plate of sea-turtle shell, dark green and ribbed like a hull. It sheds water, floats, and turns a spear with ease.

materials.name: Archelon Flipper Sinew
materials.desc: Long, rubbery tendons from a front flipper that never go slack in water. Used for straps and bindings on anything meant to be swum with.

materials.name: Bulette Armour Plate
materials.desc: A wedge of blue-grey 'landshark' plate as thick as a thumb, dense as iron but a third the weight. The classic stuff of monster-hunters' shields.

materials.name: Bulette Burrowing Gland
materials.desc: A gritty, fist-sized gland behind the jaw that secretes a soil-loosening slurry. Smells of wet clay and rust.

materials.name: Hippopotamus Ivory Tusk
materials.desc: A heavy, curved lower tusk of creamy ivory, harder than elephant ivory and self-sharpening where it grinds. Carvers and weaponsmiths both want it.

materials.name: Hippopotamus Hide
materials.desc: Skin two fingers thick that oozes a reddish sun-guard oil when fresh. Cures into leather hard enough for shields.

materials.name: Pteranodon Wing Membrane
materials.desc: A translucent, leathery sail stretched across a long finger-bone, surprisingly strong for its thinness. Glider-cloaks and kites are made from it.

materials.name: Pteranodon Hollow Bones
materials.desc: Paper-light, air-filled bones that whistle when blown across. Handy for flutes, whistles and glider frames.

materials.name: Riddle-Feather of a Sphinx of Wonder
materials.desc: A small golden feather whose barbs shift into faint lettering when read by candlelight. Scribes swear quills cut from it guess the next word before you do.

materials.name: Tear of a Sphinx of Wonder
materials.desc: A single warm, honey-bright drop that glows faintly and hums when a question is asked near it. Charm-makers treasure it for luck and flashes of insight.

materials.name: Crawling-Claw Hand Bones
materials.desc: A clattering bag of finger and wrist bones that still twitch faintly when handled. Necromancers and charm-carvers find endless uses for them.

materials.name: Crawling-Claw Grave-Dust
materials.desc: Grey, cold dust that sifts from the severed hands as the animating curse leaves them. It clings to skin like frost and numbs whatever it touches.

materials.name: Troll-Limb Knitting Flesh
materials.desc: Grey-green muscle that slowly crawls back together when cut, smelling of swamp and wet iron. Healers render it into salves; the brave eat it.

materials.name: Goblin Boss's Knucklebone Rattle
materials.desc: A gourd stuffed with teeth and knucklebones on a stick, shaken to drive minions forward. Carvers reuse the polished bones.

materials.name: Goblin Minion's Crude Javelin
materials.desc: A fire-hardened stick with a sharpened tip and a hopeful chicken feather. The seasoned shaft is still decent wood.

materials.name: Hobgoblin Captain's War Horn
materials.desc: A banded horn whose blasts carry drilled commands across a battlefield. Its brassy note still makes soldiers stand straighter.

materials.name: Bugbear Stalker's Hush Cowl
materials.desc: A shaggy, soot-dyed hood lined with moss that seems to swallow sound. Stalkers wear them until they stink of the forest floor.

materials.name: Guard Captain's Signal Horn
materials.desc: A brass-capped ox-horn stamped with the city arms, used to call the watch to arms. Loud enough to wake a barracks.

materials.name: Pirate's Belaying Pin
materials.desc: A salt-hardened hardwood pin, worn smooth by rope and handy as a cudgel. Good seasoned timber for small work.

materials.name: Pirate Captain's Treasure Chart
materials.desc: A water-stained sea chart with a hand-inked cove, soundings, and one smudged X. Cartographers and fortune-hunters both pay for it.

materials.name: Tough Boss's Weighted Cudgel
materials.desc: A hickory club with a lead core and notches for every debt collected. The wood is dense and beautifully seasoned.

materials.name: Vampire Familiar's Sigil Ring
materials.desc: A cold iron ring bearing its master's crest, worn smooth on the inside. It still tugs faintly toward the vampire it binds.

monsters.name: Stirge
monsters.blurb: A mosquito-winged bat-thing that clamps on and drinks; its tube-beak and gorged belly are what alchemists pay for.

harvest.note: Snap it off at the base, not midway: a cracked tube leaks and is useless for siphoning.
Tie off both ends before cutting. A freshly fed stirge's bladder bursts easily (fail by 5+) and sprays you with someone else's blood.

monsters.name: Allosaurus
monsters.blurb: A fast-striding predator that sprints down prey and pins it with its feet; its claws and teeth are prized trophies.

harvest.note: Rock each tooth out of its socket; prying sideways snaps the root.
Take the inner claws of the hind feet; the outer ones are too blunted.

monsters.name: Ankylosaurus
monsters.blurb: A walking fortress of bone plates with a tail that ends in a wrecking ball; armourers covet the lot.

harvest.note: Cut through the stiffened tail at the last flexible joint; it takes an hour and a saw. Dropping the club (fail by 5+) crushes a foot for 2d6 bludgeoning.
Only the back plates are thick enough; the flank studs crumble when levered free.

monsters.name: Archelon
monsters.blurb: A giant, ancient sea turtle whose shell plates are the finest waterproof armour-stuff the sea offers.

harvest.note: Separate the plates along their seams while the body is still wet; dry shell cracks when levered.

monsters.name: Bulette
monsters.blurb: The 'landshark': a burrowing armoured predator that erupts under its prey; its plates are legendary shield-stock.

harvest.note: The dorsal crest plates are best. Chisel along the growth ridges; a split plate is only good for scale mail.
Keep it damp. Nick it (fail by 5+) and the slurry sets like mortar on your hands (DC 12 Strength to free them).

monsters.name: Hippopotamus
monsters.blurb: A river-bank titan with a temper to match; its ivory and armour-thick hide repay the danger.

harvest.note: Cut the tusks out of the jaw, don't break them; half the length sits inside the bone.
Needs two people and a day; the hide must be salted at once or it rots from the inside.

monsters.name: Pteranodon
monsters.blurb: A crested, fish-snatching glider of sea cliffs; its wing membranes are the lightest sailcloth a hunter can take.

harvest.note: Cut along the finger-bone and the body wall; any tear spreads when the membrane is stretched.

monsters.name: Sphinx of Wonder
monsters.blurb: A tiny winged sphinx that guards secrets and loves a good riddle; its gifts are only worth anything if freely given.

harvest.note: Only shed or given freely, often as a prize for a clever answer. A feather torn from a slain sphinx is dull, ordinary plumage.
Shed only when a riddle's answer truly delights it or a sorrow moves it; catch the drop in a crystal phial. It cannot be taken from the dead.

monsters.name: Swarm of Crawling Claws
monsters.blurb: A skittering carpet of animated severed hands; when it finally stills, the bones and grave-dust are the prize.

harvest.note: Crush the knuckles of each hand first; unbroken ones sometimes crawl back out of the sack by night.
Sweep it up within the hour on a cloth soaked in holy water or it drifts away on the first draught.

monsters.name: Troll Limb
monsters.blurb: A hacked-off troll arm or leg that keeps grabbing and clawing on its own; the flesh never quite stops trying to heal.

harvest.note: Sear the cut ends with a torch as you butcher; unseared flesh creeps off the block and tries to rejoin its body.

monsters.name: Goblin Boss
monsters.blurb: A sly goblin warlord who hides behind its minions; its rattle and hoard are the loot.

monsters.name: Goblin Minion
monsters.blurb: The expendable rank and file of a goblin band, carrying little more than a sharpened stick.

monsters.name: Hobgoblin Captain
monsters.blurb: A disciplined goblinoid officer who drills its troops by horn-call; its kit is well kept.

monsters.name: Bugbear Stalker
monsters.blurb: A bugbear hunter-assassin that stalks from shadow; its sound-swallowing cowl is its trademark.

monsters.name: Guard Captain
monsters.blurb: A seasoned watch commander in good armour, carrying the horn that summons the garrison.

monsters.name: Pirate
monsters.blurb: A swaggering deckhand-raider; rope, a belaying pin and whatever coin it hasn't drunk.

monsters.name: Pirate Captain
monsters.blurb: A flamboyant ship's master with a spyglass, a heavy purse and a chart to something buried.

harvest.note: Usually sewn into a coat lining or hidden in a boot heel; a careless search tears it.

monsters.name: Tough Boss
monsters.blurb: A gang boss who rules the street by fist and cudgel; its purse is heavy with protection money.

monsters.name: Vampire Familiar
monsters.blurb: A living mortal sworn to a vampire's service, marked by its master's sigil ring.

harvest.note: The ring is ice-cold; wrap it before pocketing or the vampire may sense who took it.
